title: Feature format
explanation: A feature file is a stable list of requirements with a fixed shape: the four sections, an identifier per requirement, one requirement per bullet, no task status, and a dependency list that matches the references.

cases.original: Every feature must contain these sections in order:
cases.note: One rule covers every required section; the extractor reports each section's presence.
cases.suggestion: Keep the section list; the rule reads it as a checklist.

cases.original: Give every top-level requirement a stable identifier, `<FEATURE-NAME>-R<NNN>`, prefixed to the bullet.
cases.note: The extractor classifies the identifier shape; the rule refuses a malformed one. Stability over time is not checkable from one snapshot.
cases.suggestion: Say "identifiers are never renumbered; add a new one instead".

cases.original: Each requirement must be stated as a separate bullet.
cases.note: The extractor reports whether a requirement spans more than one bullet.
cases.suggestion: Keep one requirement per bullet, and give each its own identifier.

cases.original: Do not include TODO status, task sequencing, or response-format instructions in a feature file.
cases.note: The extractor reports TODO mentions; task sequencing and response-format instructions are left to review.
cases.suggestion: Say "a feature file states requirements only; status and sequencing belong elsewhere".

cases.original: A feature's `Dependencies` section names the features it requires, by file reference.
cases.note: A join between the dependency facts and the Dependencies section entries.
cases.suggestion: Name each dependency by its file path in the Dependencies section.
